_comment: SET C OF THE OPENGL ACTIVATION: the draw path itself - gfxPacket::Draw's two overloads.
IT IS EMPTY, AND THAT IS THE FINDING RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. Three separate things have to
be true before a single symbol can move into 'ported' here, and none of them is true today.
WHAT THIS WAVE IS FOR. docs/gfx_layouts.md §15 established, by walking every PROC in
game.asm.pristine for symbol references, that gfxPipeline::Draw, DrawIdx, DrawVB, DrawIdxVB,
Render and RenderIdx have ZERO CALLERS, and so does the whole gfxPipeline vertex-buffer
creation path. They are dead code in the retail image. Every triangle MM2 actually draws goes
through gfxPacket::Draw calling lpD3DDev directly:
?Draw@gfxPacket@@QBEXI@Z               0x004B3340   0x160 bytes   4 branches
?Draw@gfxPacket@@QBEXPBVMatrix44@@I@Z  0x004B34E0   0x3C0 bytes   the CPU skinning path
Both are transcribed from the machine code in code/midtown2/agigl/glgfxpacket.cpp, on top of
the FVF decode, CPU skin and GL submit in code/midtown2/agigl/glpacket.cpp.
REASON 1 - IT IS A ONE-WAY DOOR, AND IT CANNOT CARRY A -gl BRANCH.
The rule the whole activation design rests on is that a function may carry the runtime -gl
branch only if its ORIGINAL body contains no DirectDraw or Direct3D call, because the else arm
is not the original machine code - it is a fresh retyping of it against COM vtables this build
has no headers for, and it has to be right first time. Both overloads fail that test at four
sites: `mov ecx, [0x6830c8]` at 0x004B335B, `mov eax, [0x6830c8]` at 0x004B3441 and 0x004B3470,
and `mov ecx, [0x6830c8]` at 0x004B386A. So registering either one replaces the D3D7 draw path
for EVERY run, with -gl and without it. There is no half-step and no A/B test.
REASON 2 - NEITHER OVERLOAD IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT A FRAME NEEDS.
Neither Draw touches a gfxTexture, a gfxMaterial, a light, a transform or a render state. All
of that is set before the call, by modStatic::Draw, gfxRenderState::DoFlush and
gfxViewport::DoFlush, and all three dereference lpD3DDev themselves. Registering the two Draws
alone under -gl produces geometry drawn into whatever GL state happened to be left behind, and
a null dereference in the first render-state flush of the frame. The complete list - every
function in the image that reads lpD3DDev, produced by matching every absolute dword in every
section against 0x006830C8 - is in docs/opengl_activation.md, 'Set C'. It is 49 owners, of
which 30 are live.
REASON 3 - TWO PREREQUISITES OUTSIDE THIS FILE, BOTH ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN.
a. data/layouts.json says sizeof(gfxMaterial) is 0x44 and it is 0x48, proven four ways
(docs/gfx_layouts.md §7, §12, §20). modShader::AddStaticMaterial strides a pool of them,
so the wrong size is live corruption rather than a cosmetic error, and modStatic::Draw -
which is in the set - reads material+0x0C to decide alpha blending. The hand edit is
still outstanding.
b. data/layouts.json's gfxPacket carries four wrong member NAMES at 0x08, 0x14, 0x16 and
0x28, so tools/genheaders.py emits them into gfx/gfxpacket.h. The offsets and the size
are right; only the labels lie. 0x16 is the dangerous one - it is an INDEX count and both
layouts.json and MM2Hook call it TriCount, so their agreement is not corroboration.
agigl/glpacket.h works around this with a mirrored struct and a static_assert per offset,
which is why the port is not blocked on the edit; but the generated header should still
be fixed before anyone else reads it. docs/gfx_layouts.md §16.1 has the evidence and
data/layouts_gfx_round3.json records it under pending_hand_edits.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THIS WAVE, AND WHY THE SET IS FINITE AT ALL.
?AllocateVertexBuffer@gfxPacket@@IAEXXZ   0x004B43E0   lpD3D->CreateVertexBuffer
?DoLock@gfxPacket@@IAEXXZ                 0x004B4720   IDirect3DVertexBuffer7::Lock
?DoUnlock@gfxPacket@@IAEXXZ               0x004B4740
?Persist@gfxPacket@@KAPAEPAUIDirect3DVertexBuffer7@@IPAXI@Z
?ReserveVertexBuffer@gfxPacket@@SAXII@Z
?RestoreAllVertexBuffers@gfxPacket@@SAXXZ
?FreeAllVertexBuffers@gfxPacket@@SAXXZ
None of these has to be ported, because none of them RUNS. The gfxPacket constructor calls
AllocateVertexBuffer only when the packet has no matrix indices AND useNativeVBs is set
(`test al, al` on argument 10 at 0x004B38E1, then `mov al, [0x6844F8]` at 0x004B38E5).
useNativeVBs is written in exactly one function in the whole image - gfxPipeline::BeginGfx3D -
which under -gl is replaced by agiGLBeginGfx3D, and agiGLBeginGfx3D now clears it. With it
clear the constructor writes StartVertex = 0xFFFF at 0x004B3A97 instead, every packet is on
the system-memory path, and the whole vertex-buffer half of gfxPacket is unreachable. The same
call clears sm_UseInternal, which is what makes the internal-rasteriser branch unreachable.
THAT IS THE SINGLE MOST LOAD-BEARING FACT IN THIS WAVE. Without it the crash is not in a draw
at all: it is lpD3D->CreateVertexBuffer on a null lpD3D inside the gfxPacket CONSTRUCTOR, at
model load time, long before any frame.
?DrawList@gfxPacket@@SAXPBVgfxPacketList@@@Z   0x004B4870   0x70 bytes
?MakeList@gfxPacket@@SAPAVgfxPacketList@@PAV1@@Z
Neither of these needs registering either, and for a different reason: they contain no COM.
MakeList returns its argument unchanged. DrawList is a nine-instruction loop over the Next
chain that calls ?Draw@gfxPacket@@QBEXI@Z through a rel32 to the mangled symbol, so once that
symbol is ours, DrawList's untouched 1999 machine code calls straight into the C++.
TO ENABLE, IN THIS ORDER:
1. Everything in data/ported_agigl.json's second wave first - Set A and Set B. A draw call
into a frame loop that never began is not a test of anything.
2. The gfxMaterial 0x44 -> 0x48 hand edit in data/layouts.json, and regenerate headers.
3. -DARTS_AGIGL_PACKET in tools/build.py. glpacket.cpp compiles under -DARTS_AGIGL alone and
should be compiling already; this guard turns on glgfxpacket.cpp, the file that claims the
retail names.
4. Flip the two Draw declarations in gfx/gfxpacket.h from ARTS_IMPORT to ARTS_EXPORT, via
data/ported.json - tools/asm.py works from the header markers, not from this file.
5. Move the two symbols below out of this comment and into 'ported' here AND into
data/ported.json, together with the rest of Set C. Never one of the two on its own:
modModel::Draw picks between them per packet, so a half-registered pair means half the
model draws through C++ and half through machine code that no longer exists.
?Draw@gfxPacket@@QBEXI@Z
?Draw@gfxPacket@@QBEXPBVMatrix44@@I@Z
See docs/opengl_activation.md, 'Set C - one frame of geometry'.
